summary: Backend-only verification for iteration 7: new telegram_bot router (webhook + /get + /download/extension), admin dashboard surface regression (stats/codes/hits/broadcast/news), and static file greps for the extension source. Full pytest suite: 87/87 pass (58 pre-existing baseline + 15 new telegram_bot tests + 14 new admin dashboard surface tests). All requested items verified end-to-end including external-URL download of the 1,003,547-byte extension zip with valid PK ZIP magic.
critical_code_review_comments: routes/telegram_bot.py:telegram_webhook (lines 102-146) — correctly always returns {ok:true} 200 for every input (empty body, malformed JSON, missing chat_id, downstream Telegram API failure). Uses try/except at both the JSON-parse and command-dispatch layers, matching Telegram's Bot API requirement that webhooks never retry. @BotName suffix stripping is done via `first_token.split('@',1)[0].lower()` — correct for group-chat mentions.

routes/telegram_bot.py:_find_extension_zip (lines 35-45) — Searches EXTENSION_ZIP_CANDIDATES ('/app/semex-v2.2.0.zip', '/app/semex.zip') first, then falls back to glob /app/semex*.zip. Works: current build sits at /app/semex-v2.2.0.zip (1,003,547 bytes). Consider excluding /app/semex-backend.zip from the glob fallback (currently would match if the primary is missing) — minor, no user-facing impact right now.

routes/telegram_bot.py:_cmd_get (lines 75-99) — reads the entire zip into memory before send_document. At ~1MB this is fine, but if the extension grows past ~50MB Telegram's sendDocument limit will be hit — should add a size guard + friendly error before then.

services/telegram.py:send_document (lines 72-77) — correctly uses multipart/form-data via httpx `files=` param with 'application/zip' MIME. Uses shared _post() which swallows non-200 responses and returns None, so the caller (_cmd_get) correctly detects failure via `r and r.get('ok')`.

routes/admin.py — all endpoints exercised by popup.js loadAdminExtras (/stats, /codes GET+POST+DELETE, /hits, /news POST+DELETE, /broadcast + /broadcast/preview) confirmed 200 for admin token and 403 for active-user token. ObjectId path-parameters (/codes/{id}, /news/{id}) correctly validated with try/except → HTTPException(400,'Bad id').
test_credentials: Reused conftest fixtures: 999000222=active, 999000111=expired, 999000333=promoted-admin, admin_by_id_user uses settings.ADMIN_TELEGRAM_ID=5762701937.
seed_data_creation: test_admin_dashboard_surface.py generates 1 redeem code + 1 news post per test-run and deletes them within the same test. No permanent seed data.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Full backend suite: `cd /app/backend && python -m pytest tests/ -q --junitxml=/app/test_reports/pytest/pytest_results.xml` — 87 tests, ~46s. Telegram webhook tests hit downstream Telegram API against fake chat IDs — they will log warnings in the backend log about 'Telegram sendMessage failed: 400' etc, which is EXPECTED behavior (proves the webhook fault-tolerance handles downstream 400s gracefully). Do NOT change the tests to mock these — the whole point is proving that failures don't propagate as non-200 from our webhook.
rca of the issue: N/A — new-feature verification. Iteration 7 findings: (1) NEW POST /api/telegram/webhook — 200 {ok:true} for empty/malformed/all commands (/start /help /get /foobar /get@BotName /edited_message /no_chat_id) — 10 test cases all pass. (2) NEW GET /api/telegram/download/extension — external URL returns 200 application/zip, 1,003,547 bytes, first 4 bytes = PK\x03\x04, no auth required. (3) Regression: 58/58 baseline pytest still passes. (4) Extension source /app/semex/utils/server-client.js has `const POOLS = {` at line 342 with all 10 country keys (US/UK/CA/AU/DE/FR/IT/ES/NL/SE) — the /app/semex-build/ version is obfuscated so the literal 'POOLS = {' string is NOT present there, but this is expected (build.sh runs a JS obfuscator; identifier names are mangled while HTML ids/values are preserved). Zero occurrences of the old 'Vincenzo Davis' in either source or build. (5) /app/semex/popup/dashboard.html has all 9 required ids (admin-stats-grid, codes-list, codes-generate-btn, all-hits-list, broadcast-message, broadcast-send-btn, news-title, news-post-btn, news-list-admin) inside the <div id='admin-tab'> panel; ids verified to appear at file offsets > admin-tab's start offset. (6) /app/semex/popup/popup.js line 3639-3640: `window.loadAdminExtras = async function () { await Promise.allSettled([loadStats(), loadCodes(), loadAllHits(), loadNewsAdmin()]); }` — matches spec exactly. (7) /app/backend/server.py imports telegram_bot_router (line 18) and includes it (line 57). (8) /app/backend/routes/telegram_bot.py contains both `async def _cmd_get(` and `async def telegram_webhook(`.
